open_obligations: Check what data the production-grade Claude 4 Opus reward model used for evaluation was trained on; the cited passage does not say.
Check whether any human supervision entered via the task description or the RL environments.
Check the lower math and code scores before claiming parity on helpfulness.
in.other_title: Assistant RL-trained on unsupervised-label reward model matches human-supervised counterpart on average on RewardBench
in.rationale: Bai et al. leave open whether helpfulness and instruction-following can be achieved without human feedback. Wen et al. label 5,000 'more helpful, harmless, and honest' pairs with ICM, train a reward model and run RL for 250,000 episodes, reporting the assistant matches its human-label counterpart on average (higher chat and safety, lower math and code); scoring used a production-grade Claude 4 Opus reward model.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether an assistant can be trained for helpfulness without human preference labels, using an unsupervised reward model on a Claude 4 Sonnet base

text: The authors note that removing human harmlessness labels moves them closer to a self-supervised approach to alignment but that they still relied on human helpfulness labels, and leave open whether helpfulness and instruction-following can be achieved without human feedback, starting from a pretrained LM and extensive prompting.
title: Open question: helpfulness and instruction-following without any human feedback
